source.scope: Reviewed the complete 7:38 original IBM program structure, chapter sequence, indexed transcript evidence, living-spec loop, password-reset example, version control, context, security and compliance limits.
source.freshness_reason: Selected as a normal 72-hour fallback after the protected publisher-diversity gate showed that a third Google source violated the five-organization minimum and two-per-organization cap.

read_evidence.scope: Reviewed all official chapters from the need for better specs through iterative build-validation, version control, context, security and compliance.

complete_compiler_story.summary: IBM Technology contrasts spec-driven development with waterfall by treating the specification as a living artifact rather than a frozen handoff. The November 9 video walks through short build, validate, learn, and revise cycles, including edge-case discovery. It argues that faster agent execution still needs frequent validation, without presenting the method as measured performance evidence.
complete_compiler_story.why_it_matters: Use one small feature to test the method: write explicit acceptance criteria, let the agent produce a narrow draft, validate the result immediately, then revise both specification and implementation before expanding scope or permissions.
complete_compiler_story.related_coverage: Reviewed the complete official chapter sequence and indexed transcript evidence covering waterfall handoffs, stale specifications, iterative build-validation loops, password-reset edge cases, version-controlled specs, agent context, security and compliance.

complete_compiler_story.headline: OpenAI moves emergency model shutdown into inference

source.title: Control Room
source.scope: Reviewed the complete design description, job authorization boundary, cache expiry, fail-closed behavior, workload continuity and exclusion of external serving stacks.
source.freshness_reason: Selected as a 72-hour fallback for a distinct inference-control pattern after the newer AlphaProof item filled the other Technical slot.

read_evidence.scope: Reviewed the complete design description, job authorization boundary, cache expiry, fail-closed behavior, workload continuity and exclusion of external serving stacks.

complete_compiler_story.summary: OpenAI described Control Room, an internal service that can stop model inference by job identifier while leaving the surrounding workload alive. Authorization is checked inside the inference engine, cached decisions expire within thirty-five seconds, and workloads fail closed if the control service becomes unavailable. The design does not cover external serving stacks.
complete_compiler_story.why_it_matters: For sensitive model workloads, separate emergency inference shutdown from ordinary application orchestration. Test authorization, cache expiry, service failure, and audit trails with a nonproduction job so operators know exactly what stops and what continues.
complete_compiler_story.related_coverage: Reviewed the internal authorization design, bounded cache delay, fail-closed behavior and stated serving-stack limitation.
complete_compiler_story.image_alt_intent: An inference engine receives a signed stop decision while the surrounding workload remains running under an audit trail.

complete_compiler_story.summary: Google is expanding Gemini in Gmail to more Workspace users aged eighteen and older, adding thread summaries and Help me write. complete_compiler_story.headline: Google Workspace turns team standards into reusable skills

source.title: Scale customized AI across your team with skills in Google Workspace and Workspace Studio
source.scope: Reviewed the complete rollout, creation and testing flow, copy sharing, app support, scheduled flows, Drive permissions, audit controls, language limits and settings.
source.freshness_reason: Date-only publication is handled conservatively as a normal 72-hour fallback after newer-lane comparison and full source review.

read_evidence.scope: Reviewed the complete rollout, creation and testing flow, copy sharing, app support, scheduled flows, Drive permissions, audit controls, language limits and settings.

complete_compiler_story.summary: Google Workspace is rolling out reusable skills that encode team rules, templates, and reference files across Studio, Gmail, Docs, Slides, Drive, and Chat. Teams can create, test, share, and audit copies, then invoke them manually or automatically. Sheets and Meet are excluded, English is required, and shared Drive permissions still apply.
complete_compiler_story.why_it_matters: Build one bounded skill from an approved template and reference file, test it on known examples, and share a copy with one teammate. Validate output, permissions, audit events, and update ownership before enabling automatic invocation.
complete_compiler_story.related_coverage: Reviewed creation, test, copy-sharing, invocation, scheduling, permissions, audit logging, supported surfaces and rollout constraints. Procedure: choose one recurring task, write bounded instructions, attach only needed Drive context, test on a small example, and share or schedule only after review.
complete_compiler_story.image_alt_intent: A team template and reference file flow into a reusable skill, test examples, audit events and a controlled shared copy.

audience_fit.intended_user: Workspace teams that repeat document, email, and coordination tasks without writing code.
audience_fit.practical_action: Create one skill from a recurring task, attach only necessary files, and test it on a small example.
audience_fit.review_action: Inspect the generated draft, permissions, source use, and schedule before sharing or enabling broader use.
audience_fit.usable_outcome: A reusable team instruction with bounded inputs, visible review, and a controlled handoff.

complete_compiler_story.agent_skills_evidence: Reusable five-step procedure grounded in Google's documented skill builder and Workspace Studio flow: choose one recurring task, write bounded instructions, attach only needed Drive context, test on a small example, then share a copy or schedule a flow only after human review.

complete_compiler_story.headline: A marketing-agent demo keeps humans over data, claims and spend

source.title: AI Agents are too good at marketing now
source.scope: Reviewed the complete timestamped episode description and transcript evidence covering warehouse data, platform access, creative tools, ads, reference libraries and creative-director review.
source.freshness_reason: Selected as a 72-hour fallback for a distinct noncoding marketing workflow after the newer Workspace Skills story filled the dedicated Skills slot.

read_evidence.scope: Reviewed the complete timestamped episode description and transcript evidence covering warehouse data, platform access, creative tools, ads, reference libraries and creative-director review.

complete_compiler_story.summary: Greg Isenberg and Cody Schneider demonstrate a marketing-agent environment built from warehouse data, advertising APIs, creative tools, a reference library, and a reviewing agent. They create static and avatar ads during the episode. Costs and performance claims are presenter-reported, while platform permissions and human creative review remain consequential controls.
complete_compiler_story.why_it_matters: Start with read-only campaign data and one low-risk creative brief. Require a human creative director to review brand fit, permissions, claims, and platform settings before any ad is published or budget is changed.
complete_compiler_story.related_coverage: Reviewed the full timestamped workflow, keeping cost and performance claims attributed and preserving human review plus platform-permission limits.
complete_compiler_story.image_alt_intent: A marketing manager reviews agent-made ads beside read-only campaign data, permission controls and a locked budget switch.

audience_fit.intended_user: Marketing teams evaluating draft-only agent workflows without granting autonomous publishing or spending authority.
audience_fit.practical_action: Pilot one read-only campaign brief using approved reference material and narrow tool permissions.
audience_fit.review_action: Require a named creative director to verify claims, targeting, and assets before any publication or spend.
audience_fit.usable_outcome: A bounded marketing draft process with explicit evidence, permission, and release checkpoints.
